rovaniemi.text: Rovaniemi is a city in Finland and the regional capital of Lapland. It is located near the Arctic Circle in the northern interior of the country.
rovaniemi.title: Rovaniemi

santa-claus-village.text: Santa Claus Village is an amusement park in Rovaniemi, a city in the Lapland region of Finland. It was opened in 1980.
santa-claus-village.title: Santa Claus Village

sodankyla-old-church.text: Sodankylä Old Church is a 17th-century wooden church located near the Kitinen River in the Sodankylä municipality in Lapland, Finland.
sodankyla-old-church.title: Sodankylä Old Church

pyha-luosto-national-park.text: Pyhä-Luosto National Park is a national park in Lapland, Finland. It was established in 2005 when Finland's oldest national park, Pyhätunturi National Park, was joined to Luosto.
pyha-luosto-national-park.title: Pyhä-Luosto National Park

tankavaara.text: Tankavaara is a village and a tourist attraction in the municipality of Sodankylä in Lapland, Finland. It is located by the E75 highway 90 kilometres (56 mi) north of Sodankylä and 30 kilometres (19 mi) south of the Saariselkä ski resort.
tankavaara.title: Tankavaara

urho-kekkonen-national-park.text: Urho Kekkonen National Park is a national park in Lapland, Finland, situated in area of municipalities of Savukoski, Sodankylä and Inari. Established in 1983 and covering 2,550 square kilometres (985 sq mi), it is one of Finland's largest protected areas.
urho-kekkonen-national-park.title: Urho Kekkonen National Park

siida.text: A siida is an organisation of humans traditionally present in Sámi societies consisting of several families of reindeer herders whose reindeer graze together.
siida.title: Siida

sajos.text: Sajos is a Sámi cultural and administrative centre, located on the banks of the Juutuanjoki in Inari, Finland and is the largest convention and event venue in northern Lapland.
sajos.title: Sajos

lake-inari.text: Lake Inari is the largest lake in Sápmi and the third-largest lake in Finland. It is located in the northern part of Lapland, north of the Arctic Circle.
lake-inari.title: Lake Inari

kevo-strict-nature-reserve.text: Kevo Strict Nature Reserve is a strict nature reserve located in Utsjoki, northern Lapland, Finland. It was established in 1956 and covers 712 square kilometres (275 mi2).
kevo-strict-nature-reserve.title: Kevo Strict Nature Reserve

alta-museum.text: The World Heritage Rock Art Centre - Alta Museum is located in Alta Municipality in Finnmark county, Norway.
alta-museum.title: World Heritage Rock Art Centre - Alta Museum

alta-canyon.text: Sautso, also referred as Alta Canyon, is a canyon (valley) along the river Altaelva in Finnmark county, Norway. The valley is located in Alta Municipality, just north of the border with Kautokeino Municipality.
alta-canyon.title: Sautso

lyngen-alps.text: The Lyngen Alps are a mountain range in northeastern Troms county in Norway, east of the city of Tromsø. The mountain range is located on the Lyngen Peninsula and it runs through Lyngen Municipality, Balsfjord Municipality, Storfjord Municipality, and Tromsø Municipality.
lyngen-alps.title: Lyngen Alps

fjellheisen.text: Fjellheisen is an aerial tramway in Tromsø, Norway.
fjellheisen.title: Fjellheisen

arctic-cathedral.text: Tromsdalen Church or the Arctic Cathedral is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Tromsø Municipality in Troms county, Norway. It is located in the Tromsdalen valley on the east side of Tromsø.
arctic-cathedral.title: Arctic Cathedral

senja.text: Senja (Norwegian) or Sážžá (Northern Sami) is an island in Senja Municipality in Troms county, Norway in northern Europe. With an area of 1,586.3 square kilometres (612.5 sq mi), it is the second largest island in Norway.
senja.title: Senja

bleik.text: Bleik is a fishing village in Andøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway.The village is located on the northwestern part of the island of Andøya, about 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) southwest of the village of Andenes.
bleik.title: Bleik

andenes.text: (Norwegian) or Ánddanjárga (Northern Sami) is the administrative centre of Andøy Municipality which is located in the Vesterålen district of Nordland county, Norway. The village of Andenes is the northernmost settlement of the island of Andøya.
andenes.title: Andenes

svolvaer.text: Svolvær, Suolvearra (Northern Sami), or Spålavuolle (Lule Sami) is a town and the administrative centre of Vågan Municipality in Nordland County, Norway. It is located on the island of Austvågøya in the Lofoten archipelago, along the Vestfjorden.
svolvaer.title: Svolvær

vagan-church.text: Vågan Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Vågan Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located in the village of Kabelvåg on the island of Austvågøya.
vagan-church.title: Vågan Church

henningsvaer.text: Henningsvær is a fishing village in Vågan Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located on several small islands off the southern coast of the large island of Austvågøya in the Lofoten archipelago.
henningsvaer.title: Henningsvær

nusfjord.text: Nusfjord is a fishing village in Flakstad Municipality in Lofoten in Nordland county, Norway. The village lies on the southern shore of the island of Flakstadøya, along the Vestfjorden.
nusfjord.title: Nusfjord

hamnoy.text: Hamnøya is a small fishing village in Moskenes Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is located on a small peninsula on the eastern side of the island of Moskenesøya, about 1.5 kilometres (0.93 mi) northeast of the village of Reine, along the Vestfjorden.
hamnoy.title: Hamnøya

lofotr-viking-museum.text: The Lofotr Viking Museum is a historical museum based on a reconstruction and archaeological excavation of a Viking chieftain's village on the island of Vestvågøya in the Lofoten archipelago in Nordland county, Norway.
lofotr-viking-museum.title: Lofotr Viking Museum

kjerringoy.text: Kjerringøy is a village in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. The village is located about 30 kilometres (19 mi) north of the town of Bodø, along the Karlsøyfjorden, just south of the entrance to the Folda fjord.
kjerringoy.title: Kjerringøy

saltstraumen.text: Saltstraumen (Norwegian) or Stuorstrávve (Lule Sami) is a small strait with one of the strongest tidal currents in the world. It is located in Bodø Municipality in Nordland county, Norway.
saltstraumen.title: Saltstraumen

saltfjelletsvartisen-national-park.text: Saltfjellet–Svartisen National Park is a national park in Nordland county in Norway. It is located within the municipalities of Beiarn, Meløy, Rana, Rødøy, Saltdal, and Bodø.
saltfjelletsvartisen-national-park.title: Saltfjellet–Svartisen National Park

petter-dass-museum.text: The Petter Dass Museum in Alstahaug Municipality, Norway is a museum dedicated to the priest and poet Petter Dass.
petter-dass-museum.title: Petter Dass Museum

torghatten.text: Torghatten is a granite dome on the island of Torget in Brønnøy Municipality in Nordland county, Norway. It is known for its characteristic hole, or natural tunnel, through its centre.
torghatten.title: Torghatten

nidaros-cathedral.text: Nidaros Cathedral is a Church of Norway cathedral located in the city of Trondheim in Trøndelag county.
nidaros-cathedral.title: Nidaros Cathedral

munkholmen.text: Munkholmen is an islet in Trondheim Municipality in Trøndelag county, Norway. The 13,000-square-metre (3.2-acre) island sits in the Trondheimsfjord about 1.3 kilometres (0.81 mi) northwest of the island of Brattøra and the mouth of the river Nidelva in the center of the city of Trondheim.
munkholmen.title: Munkholmen

atlantic-ocean-road.text: The Atlantic Ocean Road or the Atlantic Road is an 8.3-kilometer (5.2 mi) long section of County Road 64 that runs through an archipelago that crosses Hustadvika Municipality and Averøy Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway.
atlantic-ocean-road.title: Atlantic Ocean Road

alesund.text: Ålesund is a town in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. The town is the administrative centre of Ålesund Municipality.
alesund.title: Ålesund

trollveggen.text: The Troll Wall is part of the mountain massif Trolltindene in the Romsdalen valley in Rauma Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located to the south of the towns of Åndalsnes and Molde inside the Reinheimen National Park.
trollveggen.title: Troll Wall

trollstigen.text: Trollstigen is a serpentine mountain road and pass in Rauma Municipality, Møre og Romsdal County, Norway.
trollstigen.title: Trollstigen

geiranger.text: Geiranger is a small tourist village in Sunnmøre region of Møre og Romsdal county in the western part of Norway. It is located in Stranda Municipality and at the end of the Geirangerfjorden, which is a branch of the large Storfjorden.
geiranger.title: Geiranger

dalsnibba.text: Dalsnibba is a mountain in Stranda Municipality in Møre og Romsdal county, Norway. It is located at the end of the Geiranger valley, about 7 km (4 mi) south of the village of Geiranger and the Geirangerfjorden.
dalsnibba.title: Dalsnibba

briksdalsbreen.text: Briksdalsbreen is one of the most accessible and best known arms of the Jostedalsbreen glacier. Briksdalsbreen is located in Stryn Municipality in Vestland county, Norway.
briksdalsbreen.title: Briksdalsbreen

urnes-stave-church.text: Urnes Stave Church is a 12th-century stave church at Ornes, along the Lustrafjorden, in Luster Municipality in Vestland county, Norway.
urnes-stave-church.title: Urnes Stave Church

borgund-stave-church.text: Borgund Stave Church is a former parish church initially of the Catholic Church and later the Church of Norway in Lærdal Municipality in Vestland county, Norway.
borgund-stave-church.title: Borgund Stave Church

stegastein.text: Stegastein is a scenic overlook on Sogn og Fjordane County Road 243 in Norway. The 30-metre (98 ft) long and 4-metre (13 ft) wide platform of steel and laminated pine overlooks Aurlandsvangen and the Aurlandsfjord.
stegastein.title: Stegastein

flam-line.text: The Flåm Line is a 20.2-kilometer (12.6 mi) long railway line between Myrdal and Flåm in Aurland Municipality, in Vestland county, Norway. A branch line of the Bergen Line, it runs through the valley of Flåmsdalen and connects the mainline with Sognefjord.
flam-line.title: Flåm Line

naeroyfjord.text: The Nærøyfjord is a fjord in Aurland Municipality in Vestland county, Norway. It is a branch of the Aurlandsfjord, itself a branch of the Sognefjord.
naeroyfjord.title: Nærøyfjord

bryggen.text: Bryggen, also known as Tyskebryggen, is a series of Hanseatic heritage commercial buildings lining up the eastern side of the Vågen harbour in the city of Bergen, Norway. Bryggen has been on the UNESCO list for World Cultural Heritage sites since 1979.
bryggen.title: Bryggen

voringsfossen.text: Vøringsfossen or Vøringen is the 83rd highest waterfall in Norway on the basis of total fall. It lies at the top of the Måbødalen valley in Eidfjord Municipality in Vestland county.
voringsfossen.title: Vøringsfossen

hardangervidda.text: Hardangervidda is a mountain plateau in central southern Norway, covering parts of Vestland, Telemark, and Buskerud counties. It is the largest plateau of its kind in Europe, with a cold year-round alpine climate, and one of Norway's largest glaciers, Hardangerjøkulen, is situated here.
hardangervidda.title: Hardangervidda

heddal-stave-church.text: Heddal Stave Church is a parish church of the Church of Norway in Notodden Municipality in Telemark county, Norway. It is located in the village of Heddal.
heddal-stave-church.title: Heddal Stave Church

vemork.text: Vemork is a hydroelectric power plant and a museum outside the town of Rjukan in Tinn Municipality in Telemark county, Norway. The plant was built by Norsk Hydro and opened in 1911, its main purpose being to fix nitrogen for the production of fertilizer.
vemork.title: Vemork

oslo-opera-house.text: The Oslo Opera House is the home of the Norwegian National Opera and Ballet, and the national opera house in Norway. The building is situated in the Bjørvika neighbourhood of central Oslo, at the head of the Oslofjord.
oslo-opera-house.title: Oslo Opera House

orebro-castle.text: Örebro Castle is a medieval castle on the Svartån in Örebro, Sweden. The castle was expanded during the rule of the House of Vasa and was extensively rebuilt around 1900.
orebro-castle.title: Örebro Castle

stockholm.text: Stockholm is the capital and most populous city of Sweden, as well as the largest urban area in the Nordic countries. Approximately 1 million people live in the municipality, with 1.6 million in the urban area, and 2.5 million in the metropolitan area.
stockholm.title: Stockholm

kadriorg-palace.text: Kadriorg Palace is an 18th-century Petrine Baroque palace in Kadriorg, Tallinn, the capital of Estonia. Both the Estonian and the German names for the palace mean "Catherine's valley".
kadriorg-palace.title: Kadriorg Palace

rummu.text: Rummu is a small borough in Lääne-Harju Parish, Harju County, northern Estonia. As of the 2011 census, the settlement's population was 1,088, of whom 288 (26.5%) were Estonians.
rummu.title: Rummu

padise-abbey.text: Padise Abbey was a former Cistercian monastery in Padise in Harju County, Estonia, settled in 1310 by the dispossessed monks of Dünamünde Abbey in Latvia. It was converted into a fortress after its dissolution in 1559 and later used as a country house until 1766.
padise-abbey.title: Padise Abbey

home2.text: Pärnu is a city in southwest Estonia. Pärnu is located 128 kilometres (80 mi) south of the Estonian capital, Tallinn, and 176 kilometres (109 mi) west of Estonia's second-largest city, Tartu.
home2.title: Pärnu
